Proof 1.2 says restriction of the adjoint bundle map to the zero section yields its Hom-bundle coefficients, but that restriction gives only the zero vector over f(p,x), losing F; coefficients must be recovered by evaluating a local frame. More seriously, 2.1 applies unrestricted manifold-valued Whitney approximation to sigma(p,x)=(x,f(p,x),F(p,x)) in the total Hom bundle over M x N. Its approximation and ambient retraction need not preserve the M-coordinate x. Step 3.1 then interprets the resulting linear map on T_(x_s)M as a map on T_xM, without an identification or base-preserving approximation. The cited relative Whitney theorem only supplies a manifold-valued approximation. A section-preserving parametric approximation (or explicit base correction and tangent transport), with joint jet continuity and injectivity control, is needed.

The concurrently revised current supplier now addresses the listed objections; this finding does not claim those defects persist in the revision. The statement allows any formal family smooth near Q, but the opened supplier lem-smoothing-formal-immersion-families requires it to be holonomic there, namely F=d_x f. Step 1.1 says smooth formal data provide the required holonomic model, which is false: smoothness does not imply this differential equation. The given Phi is also typed as a map to C^infinity(M,N), which cannot itself encode pairs in FImm. The proof must distinguish base-map and formal-pair families and prove/use smoothing relative to arbitrary smooth formal data, with the countable-choice hypothesis carried explicitly.

The proof asserts that the restriction map has contractible extension fibres by shrinking disk fibres, and then concludes that a map with contractible fibres is a weak homotopy equivalence. That implication needs a fibration/quasifibration or a direct parametric proof, none supplied for this restriction. Shrinking also changes the prescribed normal-bundle identification (vertical derivatives scale), so it is not the asserted contraction of the fixed decorated fibre. The cited Euclidean tubular theorem concerns embedded submanifolds, whereas the datum here is an arbitrary immersion into N. Francis Lectures 5-6, Lemma 1.9, PDF pp.3-4, states the decorated weak equivalence but only sketches an exponential-map section. A parametric normal-identified microextension and inverse homotopies, or an applicable proved fibration theorem, is needed to license this item and the closed-source Smale-Hirsch comparison.

findings.location: Summary, second sentence: the k-fold round circles realise every rotation number
findings.evidence: The zero-fold round-circle map is constant, with zero derivative, so it is not an immersion and has no rotation number. Only nonzero integers are realised by these round-circle immersions; the Gerono lemniscate supplies zero. This B-page prose is outside the reader edit license.
